docs.title: PyKampala Community Blog
docs.text:
Welcome to the PyKampala Community Blog — technical stories, tutorials, and community updates from Python developers in Uganda. Established 2016.

We host physical and virtual meetups every last Saturday of the month. This blog extends our main website with in-depth articles you can read, share, and discuss.

docs.title: Building Python Projects with Purpose
docs.text: Categories: Programming • Software

docs.title: Why Project Structure Matters
docs.text:
A well-structured Python project saves time, prevents bugs, and makes collaboration joyful. In this post, we explore a minimal yet scalable layout inspired by real Pykampala contributions.

A clear layout is documentation for your future self.

docs.title: A Minimal Layout
docs.text:
my_project/
├── src/
│   └── my_package/
│       ├── __init__.py
│       └── core.py
├── tests/
│   └── test_core.py
├── pyproject.toml
└── README.md

docs.title: Packaging with pyproject.toml
docs.text:
[project]
name = "my_package"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "An example Python package"
requires-python = ">=3.9"

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
def test_core():
    from my_package.core import hello
    assert hello("Kampala") == "Hello, Kampala!"

Run with:

pytest

docs.title: Building an AI Application
docs.text: This post demonstrates multiple categories. It belongs to AI and Machine-Learning, Programming, and Web — so it should appear in each category listing.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: We’ll build a simple AI-powered web app that classifies text.

docs.title: Code Example
docs.text:
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer

vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer()
X = vectorizer.fit_transform(["hello world", "machine learning"])
print(X.toarray())
